title: Recreate a Superstar in Seconds? Suno Sued Again for Infringement

content_html:
AI music generation platform Suno is once again facing a copyright infringement lawsuit. The entity that owns the music rights to Elvis Presley, along with Eight Mile Style, the music publishing company for Eminem's songs, recently formally filed a lawsuit against Suno, accusing it of using well-known artists' likenesses and works without authorization to create AI-generated songs, allegedly resulting in serious copyright infringement.

The core of this lawsuit is that content generated by Suno closely imitates legendary musicians in melody, style, and lyrics. Attorneys for the plaintiffs pointed out that such tools copy and generate similar works within seconds without years of artistic accumulation and authorization, severely undermining the legitimate rights and interests of human creators. In response, Suno said that the platform strictly prohibits the unauthorized use of specific artists' names and songs and has introduced third-party tools to screen for potential abuse.

As a focal point in the generative AI music field, Suno has previously faced multiple industry lawsuits. Earlier this year, Sony Music Entertainment and Universal Music Group jointly filed a lawsuit against it, alleging infringement by its v6 model; however, Warner Music Group recently dropped its lawsuit and reached a licensing agreement with it. Elvis Presley's rights holders had also previously filed a $41 million lawsuit against Anthropic over copyright issues related to AI model training.

Such legal disputes highlight the deep tension between the rapid development of generative AI and traditional copyright protection. As multiple copyright holders tighten their legal enforcement, the compliance boundaries of AI music generation technology are facing reconstruction, and the industry may accelerate its evolution toward standardized legal licensing and commercial cooperation in the future.
